leftSections.textContent: I'm Rebecca, representing the Ama Tours, and I extend a warm welcome to all of you in breathtaking Lombok. Are you tired after a long flight? I hope you're not. Now, let's take a moment to get acquainted with some important safety rules. First, please stay seated until we arrive at our destination and avoid eating, drinking, or standing while on the bus. leftSections.title: Question 11: Express an Opinion
leftSections.textContent: Do you agree or disagree with the practice of companies laying off older employees in order to hire new employees at lower salaries? Provide reasons and examples to support your opinion.

sampleTemplateViewModel.content: I disagree with the idea of laying off older employees to hire new ones at lower salaries. Experience and loyalty are important. Older employees bring valuable knowledge and stability to a company. For example, in my father's company, experienced workers help mentor new hires and improve productivity. Laying them off to save money can make the company lose important expertise. Instead, companies could train all employees to develop new skills and adapt to changes.

I disagree with companies laying off older employees to hire new ones at lower salaries. Firstly, experienced employees bring valuable skills and knowledge from years in the industry. Their mentoring abilities help younger colleagues and boost productivity. Secondly, firing older workers just to cut costs creates a negative atmosphere and insecurity. For instance, in a company I know, when older workers were laid off, the remaining staff felt anxious about their job security and less motivated to work. Companies should value loyalty and experience because these contribute to long-term success.
Phần trả lời chỉ nhắc lại một số cụm từ từ đề bài, và không nói hoàn thiện được một câu nêu quan điểm cá nhân.
Bạn có cố gắng nói được ở mức độ câu tuy nhiên còn ngập ngừng, lặp từ, và tự sửa lỗi nhiều lần. Phần trả lời không có sự liên kết và khiến người nghe khó hiểu.

Bạn gặp khó khăn trong việc tìm ý tưởng và từ vựng để trả lời câu hỏi đề bài. Quan điểm của bạn chỉ mới được đưa ra một cách mơ hồ ở phần đầu. Phần nói không trôi chảy. Có nhiều lỗi ngữ pháp và các cấu trúc ngữ pháp được sử dụng còn hạn chế.

Bạn đưa ra được lý do tốt để hỗ trợ quan điểm của mình và sử dụng từ vựng, ngữ pháp hiệu quả. Phần trả lời nhìn chung trôi chảy, tuy nhiên phát âm nhiều chỗ chưa tốt, sử dụng ngữ điệu không phù hợp, làm người nghe gặp khó khăn.

Bạn đưa ra được quan điểm rõ ràng, sử dụng cấu trúc và từ vựng tương đối tốt. Tốc độ nói phù hợp và phát âm rõ ràng. Mặc dù vẫn còn ảnh hưởng của ngôn ngữ mẹ đẻ nhưng không ảnh hưởng đến việc hiểu thông điệp của người nghe.

questionInfo.questionName: Directions: Respond to the email as if you are one of the Coco Trip Customer Service members. In your email, give ONE reason and make TWO compensations.

sampleTemplateViewModel.content:
Dear Amelia Archer,
Thank you for your email. I am very sorry to hear about your disappointment.
The tour was canceled because of bad weather. Safety is very important to us.
We want to make up for this. First, we can reschedule your tour to another day that works for you. You can choose any date that is good for you, and we will book the tour again for free. Second, we will give you a 20% discount on your next tour with us. You can use this discount for any other tour you book with us in the future.
Please let us know a good day for you to reschedule.
Thank you for your understanding.
Best regards, 
Coco Trip Tours

Dear Amelia Archer,
Thank you for reaching out to us. I understand your disappointment regarding the cancellation of the Statue of Liberty Tour scheduled for June 20.
Unfortunately, the tour was canceled due to severe weather conditions. Your safety is our top priority.
To compensate for this inconvenience, we would like to offer you two options. First, we can reschedule your tour for another date that suits your schedule. You may select any available date, and we will rebook the tour for you at no additional cost. Additionally, we are offering a 20% discount on your next booking with us. This discount can be applied to any future tour or experience you choose to book with Coco Trip.
Please let us know your preferred date for rescheduling, and we will make the necessary arrangements.
Thank you for your understanding and patience.
Best regards, 
Coco Trip Tours

leftSections.title: Question 8: Write an opinion essay
leftSections.textContent: For some employers, references from applicants' previous employers can be crucial for hiring decisions. Why do you think that references are important to employers? Use specific reasons and examples to explain your answer.

sampleTemplateViewModel.content:
Employers often ask for references from the places where candidates previously worked when they are looking to hire someone new. In this essay, I will talk about why these references are important during the hiring process.
Firstly, references help employers check if what the candidate says about their skills and experience is true. A good word from a past manager or coworker can prove that the candidate really has the qualifications and has done well in their past jobs. For example, if a candidate says they are good at managing projects, a reference can give examples of projects the candidate managed successfully.
Secondly, references give information about how the candidate works and what they are like as a person. Employers need this information to see if the candidate will fit well with their team. A reference can mention important qualities like being reliable, working well with others, and solving problems. For instance, a past employer might talk about how the candidate always met deadlines and worked well with others.
Furthermore, references help reduce the risk when hiring someone new. Hiring involves both a big investment and some risks. With references, employers can make better choices and avoid hiring someone who might not be right for the job, which could cause financial problems or trouble at work.
In conclusion, references from past employers are very useful when hiring. They give a detailed view of what the candidate has done professionally, confirm their abilities, and help reduce hiring risks. As jobs keep changing, the need for good references shows why it's important to have strong professional relationships and do well in your career.

References from previous employers play a crucial role in the hiring process for many employers. They provide valuable insights into a candidate’s past work performance, reliability, and overall suitability for the job. There are several reasons why references are important to employers.
Firstly, references offer a glimpse into the candidate’s work history and achievements. When an employer contacts a reference, they can verify the accuracy of the information provided in the candidate’s resume and during the interview. For example, if a candidate claims to have successfully managed a project, a reference can confirm this and provide additional details about how the candidate handled the project. This helps employers ensure that the candidate has the relevant experience and skills for the job.
Secondly, references provide insight into a candidate’s interpersonal skills and ability to work in a team. By speaking with former colleagues or supervisors, employers can learn about the candidate’s communication skills, adaptability, and how they handle conflicts or challenges in the workplace. For instance, if a reference mentions that the candidate was known for resolving team disputes effectively, it indicates that the candidate possesses strong interpersonal skills, which are valuable in any work environment.
Furthermore, references can highlight a candidate’s reliability and work ethic. Employers want to hire individuals who are dependable, punctual, and committed to their work. A reference can provide specific examples of the candidate’s attendance record, willingness to take on additional responsibilities, and overall dedication to their job. For example, if a reference mentions that the candidate often volunteered for extra tasks and consistently met deadlines, it suggests that the candidate is hardworking and dependable.
In conclusion, references from previous employers are essential for several reasons. They provide a comprehensive view of the candidate’s work history, interpersonal skills, and reliability. By obtaining this information, employers can make more informed and confident hiring decisions, ultimately leading to a more productive and harmonious workplace.
